title: Balanced derived scalar tensor coherence on perfect ring complexes
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a unital homomorphism of commutative rings. Write $\operatorname{Perf}(R)$ for the full subcategory of $D(R)$ consisting of objects isomorphic to bounded complexes of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use signed total tensor, whose differential on homogeneous tensors is $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{\deg x}x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the derived tensor product $-\otimes_R^LN$ of ordinary module complexes, computed on K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (with $N=S[0]$ for scalar extension and $N=Q$ for $P\otimes_R^LQ$), and ordinary module scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then derived scalar extension $B_{S/R}(P)=P\otimes_R^L S$ restricts to an $R$-linear additive functor $\operatorname{Perf}(R)\to\operatorname{Perf}(S)$. On a bounded finite-projective representative it is termwise scalar extension. It has natural isomorphisms
$$b_{S/R,P,Q}:B_{S/R}(P\otimes_R^LQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{S/R}(P)\otimes_S^LB_{S/R}(Q),\qquad B_{S/R}(R[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}S[0],$$
represented by $(x\otimes y)\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes1)$ and $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$. Their inverse tensor map is $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. These comparisons respect the associator, the symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg x\deg y}y\otimes x$, and both unitors. They are independent of representatives and natural for all derived morphisms, not just chain maps between fixed models.
For composable ring maps $R\to S\to T$, the natural isomorphism $c_{T/S/R}:B_{T/S}B_{S/R}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{T/R}$ is represented by $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes st$, where $s$ is mapped to $T$. For the identity ring map the comparison $B_{R/R}\cong\operatorname{id}$ is multiplication. These comparisons satisfy the unit and four-ring associativity equations, and their tensor and coefficient-unit squares with the maps $b$ commute. All assertions include identity ring maps.

source.place: Tags 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and 0GWN (section-symmetric-monoidal). Agent-formulated perfect-complex restriction and explicit coherence of the balanced maps; the full conjunction is not asserted verbatim by either source.

proof.text: Work with bounded finite-projective complexes. A finite generating list for a projective module $M$ gives a surjection $R^n\to M$; projective lifting supplies a section, so $M$ is a retract of $R^n$. Tensor the two splitting maps with $S$: their composite remains the identity, and $R^n\otimes_RS\cong S^n$ by the coordinate maps. Thus $M\otimes_RS$ is finite projective. Likewise tensoring splittings for $M$ and $N$ exhibits $M\otimes_RN$ as a retract of $R^{nm}$; a finite sum of these splittings is a splitting into a finite free module. Consequently scalar extension and signed total tensor preserve bounded finite-projective complexes; if the input bounds are $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, the tensor bounds are $[a+c,b+d]$. The same argument includes zero modules, empty generating lists and zero rings.

Every term of such a complex is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Boundedness above therefore makes it K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $N=S[0]$: the canonical K-flat computation identifies $B_{S/R}(Q_RP)$ with $Q_S(P\otimes_RS)$, including the maps induced by chain maps of $P$. With $A=R$ and $N=Q$, it also computes $Q_RP\otimes_R^LQ_RQ$ by $Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$. Step 1 applies over both $R$ and $S$, so every tensor and every iterated scalar extension occurring below has such a K-flat finite-projective model. In particular $B_{S/R}$ takes perfect objects to perfect objects, by the definition of perfect and functoriality on isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism), 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change); restriction to the models of step 1

proof.text: Let $\mathcal H_R$ have bounded finite-projective complexes as objects and chain-homotopy classes as morphisms. Localization $E_R:\mathcal H_R\to\operatorname{Perf}(R)$ is fully faithful: [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] gives exactly the required bijection on each Hom set, since its source complex is bounded above and projective. It is essentially surjective by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. In particular every derived map between these models is a chain map up to homotopy, and equality of their localized maps is equality of homotopy classes. If two models of the same perfect object are chosen, the specified derived identification between them and its inverse lift to homotopy classes; faithfulness shows their composites are identities. This also covers identifications that are not supplied by a specified quasi-isomorphism of models.

source.place: Tag 064B (lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex), applied to the full category of bounded finite-projective complexes

proof.text: Termwise scalar extension sends a chain map $f$ to $f\otimes1$ and a degree $-1$ homotopy $h$ to $h\otimes1$. Indeed $(f-g)\otimes1=(dh+hd)\otimes1=d(h\otimes1)+(h\otimes1)d$. Hence it gives a functor on $\mathcal H_R$, and $((f+g)\otimes1)=(f\otimes1)+(g\otimes1)$, $((rf)\otimes1)=r(f\otimes1)$ by [def-weil-module-base-change], where $R$ acts on the target via $R\to S$. Under step 2 this is the restriction of $B_{S/R}$. The Hom bijection of step 3 preserves addition and scalars (the scalar $r$ is composition with the localized map $r\,\mathrm{id}$), so this restriction is additive and $R$-linear on every derived Hom set.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change); elementary termwise homotopy and linearity calculation

proof.text: Signed total tensor also respects homotopy classes. For a homotopy $h$ in the first variable use $H(x\otimes y)=h(x)\otimes y$. In $dH+Hd$ the terms involving $dy$ have coefficients $(-1)^{\deg x-1}+(-1)^{\deg x}=0$, leaving $(dh+hd)(x)\otimes y$. For a homotopy $k$ in the second variable use $H(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{\deg x}x\otimes k(y)$: the terms with $dx$ cancel, leaving $x\otimes(dk+kd)(y)$. These identities and functoriality of the tensor construction give a bifunctor on $\mathcal H_R$. By step 2 and clause (3) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], it represents the derived tensor in both variables on perfect objects.

source.place: Tag 0GWN (section-symmetric-monoidal), lemma-derived-tor-homotopy; explicit homotopies in both variables

proof.text: For homogeneous $x\in P^p$, $y\in Q^q$, define $b((x\otimes y)\otimes s)=(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes1)$ and $v((x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b))=(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. These formulas extend by the balanced tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Moving $r\in R$ across $x\otimes y$ moves its image in $S$ across the target $S$-tensor, and balancing the outer $R$-tensor moves that same image into $s$. For $v$, moving $t\in S$ across the middle tensor replaces $(at)b$ by $a(tb)$, and the inner $R$-balancing gives the image of $r$ in the product $ab$. Thus both maps are well-defined and $S$-linear. We have $vb=1$. Also $bv$ sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ to $(x\otimes ab)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, which equals the original tensor by $S$-balancing. Apply these maps on every $(p,q)$ summand of the finite total complexes.

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product), balanced universal property; agent calculation of b and its inverse

proof.text: The map $b$ commutes with differentials: both $d\,b$ and $b\,d$ on $(x\otimes y)\otimes s$ equal $(dx\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes1)+(-1)^p(x\otimes s)\otimes(dy\otimes1)$. The coefficients have degree zero. Thus $b$ is a chain isomorphism, with inverse $v$. The coefficient-unit chain isomorphism is $u:R[0]\otimes_RS\to S[0]$, $r\otimes s\mapsto f(r)s$, where $f:R\to S$ is the given map; its inverse is $s\mapsto1\otimes s$, since $r\otimes s=1\otimes f(r)s$. Localization and the computation isomorphisms from step 2 give precisely the two isomorphisms asserted in the item.

For chain maps $h:P\to P'$ and $k:Q\to Q'$, the naturality square of $b$ sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes s$ along either path to $(h(x)\otimes s)\otimes(k(y)\otimes1)$. The unit map is a single coefficient morphism, and its compatibility with the scalar action is $f(rr')s=f(r)f(r')s$. Since pure tensors generate each summand, these are equalities of chain maps. Step 5 ensures these squares also hold on homotopy classes. We will pass from those classes to arbitrary derived morphisms in the final step.

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product); elementary naturality of the displayed balanced maps

proof.text: Check monoidal constraints on homogeneous generators. For the associator, the two paths from $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\otimes s$, after the target associator, both give $(x\otimes s)\otimes((y\otimes1)\otimes(z\otimes1))$. For symmetry, both paths on $(x\otimes y)\otimes s$ give $(-1)^{pq}(y\otimes1)\otimes(x\otimes s)$: the other apparent value $(-1)^{pq}(y\otimes s)\otimes(x\otimes1)$ is equal by $S$-balancing. For the left unitor, both paths on $(r\otimes x)\otimes s$ give $x\otimes f(r)s$; for the right unitor, both paths on $(x\otimes r)\otimes s$ give the same expression. Here the coefficient-unit comparison is $u$ from step 7. Tensor generation proves each diagram commutes, including negative degrees, where only the parity of $pq$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0GWN (section-symmetric-monoidal), associator, signed commutativity and unit constraints; explicit diagrams

proof.text: For $R\xrightarrow f S\xrightarrow g T$ define $c_P:(P\otimes_RS)\otimes_ST\to P\otimes_RT$ by $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes g(s)t$. Its inverse is $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. The relations hold because $g(f(r))t=(gf)(r)t$ and $g(ss')t=g(s)g(s')t$; the two composites are identities by balancing. Both maps commute with $d_P$ and with any chain map of $P$. For the identity ring map put $i_P:P\otimes_RR\to P$, $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; these are also natural chain maps and inverse by balancing. Step 2 computes the composite derived functor on this very iterated model, so these are comparison isomorphisms of the asserted derived functors once descended.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), functorial iterated base change, with explicit balanced multiplication maps

proof.text: The two ring-unit equations can be checked before localization. On $(x\otimes r)\otimes s$ for $R\xrightarrow{1}R\xrightarrow f S$, multiplication via $c$ and first using $i$ both give $x\otimes f(r)s=rx\otimes s$. On $(x\otimes s)\otimes s'$ for $R\xrightarrow f S\xrightarrow{1}S$, both give $x\otimes ss'$. For a fourth ring $T\xrightarrow h U$, the two composites from $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)\otimes u$ to $P\otimes_RU$ give respectively $x\otimes h(g(s)t)u$ and $x\otimes h(g(s))h(t)u$; these agree since $h$ preserves products. Thus the four-ring equation and both unit equations hold without excluding identity maps.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change); agent check of the four-ring and identity equations

proof.text: The tensor square for $c$ starts at $((P\otimes_RQ)\otimes_RS)\otimes_ST$. Apply $c_{P\otimes Q}$ then $b_{T/R}$ to $((x\otimes y)\otimes s)\otimes t$: the result is $(x\otimes g(s)t)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. The other path first applies $B_{T/S}(b_{S/R})$, then $b_{T/S}$, then $c_P\otimes c_Q$, giving $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)\otimes((y\otimes1)\otimes1)$ before the final map, hence the same result. The coefficient-unit square on $(r\otimes s)\otimes t$ gives $(gf)(r)g(s)t$ along both paths. For the identity comparison $i$, its tensor square on $(x\otimes y)\otimes r$ has values $(rx)\otimes y$ and $x\otimes(ry)$, equal by balancing; its coefficient-unit square is multiplication $r\otimes r'\mapsto rr'$. Thus all the required tensor and coefficient-unit squares commute on complexes.

source.place: Tags 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and 0GWN (section-symmetric-monoidal); agent check of tensor and coefficient-unit squares

proof.text: Finally use [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] to pass to perfect objects, retaining the chosen K-flat computation comparisons of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Choose for each perfect object $K$ a model $P$ with an isomorphism $e:Q_RP\to K$. Transport each comparison by its source and target functors applied to $e$ (and the corresponding $e$ for each other variable). For example the tensorator at $(K,L)$ is obtained by conjugating the tensorator at $(Q_RP,Q_RQ)$ by $B(e\otimes^Le')$ and $B(e)\otimes^LB(e')$. An arbitrary derived morphism, conjugated into these models, lifts to a chain-homotopy class by the cited bijection; the chain-map naturality squares of steps 8 and 10 therefore prove its naturality. A different choice of models is related by the unique homotopy classes lifting their derived identifications, as in step 3. Naturality for these classes makes the two transported comparisons equal; composing three such identifications gives the same result by the injectivity of the bijection. Thus the comparisons are independent of representatives. Every coherence equation from steps 9, 11 and 12 remains an equation after localization and conjugation. This proves all clauses for all derived morphisms and all ring maps.
